description: Simulator confirmed scenario: MongoDB auth failures followed by disconnect and host unreachable. How to replicate: run write_rca_test_logs_linux.py --scenario mongo_auth_chain_confirmed.

Simulator confirmed scenario: MongoDB auth failures escalate into client disconnects, nginx 502 burst, then MongoDB host unreachable. How to replicate: run write_rca_test_logs_linux.py --scenario nginx_mongodb_auth_outage_confirmed.
Detects Kafka broker shutdown/unavailability with user-facing impact. How to replicate: stop Kafka broker or block broker port, then trigger API operations depending on Kafka and observe nginx 5xx.
Detects MongoDB down/unreachable states propagating to edge failures. How to replicate: stop mongod or block MongoDB port from API host, then hit API endpoints that query DB and watch nginx 5xx.
Detects nginx service-down conditions that impact users. How to replicate: stop nginx service (or force failed unit), then send HTTP traffic and observe 5xx responses.

Detects RabbitMQ broker-down behavior affecting API/edge path. How to replicate: stop rabbitmq-server or break AMQP listener, then execute message-producing API calls and observe gateway/service unavailable errors.
Detects host/network link-down cascades across messaging, database, and edge layers. How to replicate: flap NIC or apply network drop/route blackhole, then run normal API traffic to induce timeouts.

Detects local-topology MongoDB authentication failures cascading into client disconnects, repeated nginx 502 responses, and final host-unreachable state. How to replicate: generate mongodb_auth_failed 3 times from /var/log/mongodb/mongod.log, then mongodb_interrupted_client_disconnected once, then nginx_access_502_bad_gateway 3 times from /var/log/nginx/access.log, and finally mongodb_host_unreachable once.

Single-rule dependency-cause detector for data_collector downtime using explicit sequence blocks. Step 0 uses signal_keys so any one dependency fault can start the incident. Step 1 uses all_of so the rule confirms both a data_collector-down signal and a service-manager failure signal before raising the RCA. How to replicate: trigger one dependency fault on the kafka, mongodb, postgres, or network path; then stop or crash data_collector so both data_collector_service_down and either systemd_unit_failed or systemd_watchdog_timeout appear on the same host.

Detects API to MongoDB dependency break with request timeout symptoms. How to replicate: firewall MongoDB from API node or force DB disconnects, then call DB-backed APIs and observe nginx 504 and operation interruptions.

Detects API to RabbitMQ dependency break manifested at edge. How to replicate: block AMQP between API and RabbitMQ or force broker connection resets, then run API message workflows and observe 503/5xx responses.

Detects high edge load that converges with MongoDB degradation and turns into user-visible failures. How to replicate: run high HTTP load while adding slow MongoDB queries; observe upstream timeout/read-header errors and 5xx.

Detects Kafka load/lag growth with replication or timeout faults and user-path slowdown. How to replicate: increase producer rate and/or throttle consumers to build lag, then induce broker stress and watch upstream latency.

Detects MongoDB load increase followed by database faults and edge latency/errors. How to replicate: run heavy read/write load to trigger slow commands and lock waits, then hit API endpoints and observe upstream latency/5xx.

Detects RabbitMQ load pressure escalating into broker faults and API latency. How to replicate: flood queue producers so backlog/unacked grow, then continue traffic until heartbeat/blocking appears and nginx upstream latency rises.
